newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Colonial shares list at A$3.31.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Colonial shares list at A$3.31.

text.p: Shares in insurance and banking group Colonial Ltd listed at A$3.31 on Monday, up 21 cents or 6.8 percent from the A$3.10 price set for institutional investors and up 77 cents from the A$2.60 set for the public.
Trade in Colonial's shares in New Zealand began at NZ$3.70.
The price set effectively meant Colonial's share issue was immediately valued at A$745 million, compared with the A$690 million raised.
The price had eased to A$3.25 by 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT).
Colonial closed its 235 million share offer on Friday, with institutional investors able to bid for two-thirds of those shares and the public bidding for the other third.
The A$3.10 institutional price, set on Sunday, was well above the shares' A$2.48 net asset backing.
Colonial had given an "indicative range" of between A$2.50 and A$2.90 as a guide to institutions, but on Sunday it said the limited number of shares on offer drew bids well above that.
Colonial sold shares to members of the public for a fixed price of A$2.60 each this month. Each share, for both retail and institutional shareholders, comes with an option to buy more.
Colonial managing director Peter Smedley told a news conference in Melbourne on Sunday he hoped for a premium above the institutional price.
Colonial becomes only the second life office to list on the Australian Stock Exchange, after one of its bigger rivals, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, listed last October.
Australia's biggest, the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), will soon follow. It plans to shed its old mutual structure and list in Australia and New Zealand next year.
Colonial has total assets of A$29.7 billion and is the only local life office with a bank, Sydney-based Colonial State Bank.
It will list with a register of over 500,000 shareholders, including its former Asian insurance partner, Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd, which has secured a major stake.
Colonial plans to use some of the proceeds of the float to fund its recent decision to buy out Jardine's half interest in their Asian business for US$163 million.
